cells: Details about the publisher’s app, via an App object (see App object ).
For more information, refer to the section on [`app objects`](#app).
An object describing the project or application.
Application iTunes ID or package name. On Android, this is the package name, for example com.example.app . On iOS, this is either the bundle ID or the iTunes ID, for example 628677149 .

The application bundle or package name, intended to be unique across exchanges.- Android apps pass the Bundle ID. - iOS apps pass the Bundle ID or Store ID.This attribute might not be passed in circumstances where contractual agreements with the publisher prohibit it.
IAB content categories for the Application. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 List 5.1 for details.
Object that describes the content where the impression will appear for certain requests, including CTV inventory. Aligns to OpenRTB Specification 3.2.16 .
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB, including CTV inventory.
URL of the content, for buy-side contextualization or review.
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
Indicates device orientation: portrait or landscape .
The application name.This attribute might not be passed in circumstances where contractual agreements with the publisher prohibit it.
Details about the publisher of the app.

Extension object containing more publisher information. This contains the installed_sdk object which has fields id , and subobject SDK_version with SDK bidder name and version details. For DSP bidders, id will always be "APPLOVIN_EXCHANGE" .
The publisher’s AppLovin ID. Publishers should add this value to their app-ads.txt file.
The URL for the app in the App Store or Google Play Store. Used for app-ads.txt compliance.
yes, only sent to DSP bidders
The store URL for an installed app (for QAG 1.5 compliance).This attribute might not be passed in circumstances where contractual agreements with the publisher prohibit it.
Auction type. If 1 then first-price auction; if 2 then second-price auction. Always 1 for AppLovin.
The auction type used. All Unity Exchange auctions are first-price auctions, so the value is always `1`.

Block list of advertisers by their top-level domains (for example, “ ford.com ”). A maximum of 30 domains are passed. Bids containing other domains blocked by publishers are invalidated and do not participate in the auction.
no, only sent to DSP bidders

Block list of applications by their platform-specific, exchange-independent application identifiers. On Android, these are bundle or package names (such as “ com.foo.mygame ”); on iOS, these are numeric IDs. Note: This field is sent on an opt-in basis. Contact your account manager if you want to enable this field. A maximum of 30 bundles are passed. Bids containing other bundle IDs blocked by publishers are invalidated and do not participate in the auction.
no, only sent to DSP bidders
A list of blocked applications, represented by their specific platform. On Android, these are bundle or package names. On iOS, these are numeric IDs.
Blocked IAB categories for this impression. See blocked categories for a list.
no, only sent to DSP bidders
Blocked advertiser categories, using [IAB taxonomy IDs](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/iab-category-mapping.md).This attribute is supported but optional.
Details about the user’s device to which the impression is delivered, via a Device object (see Device object ).
For more information, refer to the section on [`device objects`](#device).
An object describing the user's device.
Carrier of device on a cellular network, or ISP of device on Wi-Fi.

Type of connection 0 unknown—always 0 if the SDK signal is not present. 1 Ethernet—if device connects via Ethernet (Android only) 2 Wi-Fi—if device connects via Wi-Fi (Android / iOS) 3 Cellular—unknown connection (Android / iOS) 4 Cellular — 2G (Android / iOS) 5 Cellular — 3G (Android / iOS) 6 Cellular — 4G (Android / iOS) 7 Cellular — 5G (Android / iOS)

The network connection type. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.22** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).
The general type of device. 1 for mobile and tablets. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.21 for details.

The general type of device. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.21** in the [](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf)[OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).Note that separation between phone and tablet was introduced in in OpenRTB version 2.2:- `4` specifies a phone. - `5` specifies a tablet.
Specifies whether the “Do Not Track” feature is enabled in the device. If 0 , then DNT is false. If 1 , then DNT true. This parameter is omitted if DNT is not passed by the SDK or on iOS 5 or lower.
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
(iOS only) An integer passed to represent the app’s app tracking authorization status: 0 = not determined 1 = restricted 2 = denied 3 = authorized
IDFV of device in that publisher. Only passed when IDFA is unavailable or all zeros.
Location of the device, assumed to be the user’s current location, defined by a Geo object .
Location data for the device (assumed to be the user's current location):- `lat` - `lon` - `type` - `country` - `region` - `city` - `UTCoffset`
City of the device. Based on the IP address & Maxmind database.
Country of the device. Based on the IP address & Maxmind database. Passed as a country code using ISO-3166-1-alpha-3 .
Nielsen DMA code based on IP address.
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
Service or provider used to determine geolocation from IP address if applicable (that is, type = 2 ). Refer to List 5.23 in the OpenRTB Spec 2.5 for more details.
Language and country of the device. Example us_en signifies English as language and the United States as the country.
Zip code of the device. Based on the IP address & Maxmind database.
Region code using ISO-3166-2; two-letter state code if country is USA . Derived from IP address. See Valid region codes below.
Source of location data. Refer to List 5.20 in the OpenRTB Spec 2.5 for more details.
Height of the screen in physical pixels. This may be dependent on the device orientation. Note: This can differ from banner.h .
The hardware version of the device.

Apple IFA or Google Advertising ID. Google Advertising ID (Android) is lowercase by default; IFA (iOS) is uppercase by default. If raw is not available then this is not passed. Not passed in requests from countries subject to GDPR if the user does not give consent.

The Android Advertising ID (AID) or iOS Identifier for Advertisers (IFA/IDFA) sanctioned for advertiser use in the clear (not hashed).Unity clears this field where required by COPPA or GDPR compliance.
IPv4 address of the device. Not passed in requests from countries subject to GDPR if the user does not give consent.
The device's IP address.Unity clears this field where required by COPPA or GDPR compliance.
IPv6 address of the device. When ipv6 is present, ip is 255.255.255.255 by default. Not passed in requests from countries subject to GDPR if the user does not give consent.
1 if the device supports JavaScript; otherwise 0 . (Always 1 .)
“Limit Ad Tracking” signal commercially endorsed (for example by iOS, Android), where 0 = tracking is unrestricted, 1 = tracking must be limited per commercial guidelines

The "Limit Ad Tracking" signal that is commercially endorsed.- `0` indicates tracking is unrestricted. - `1` indicates tracking must be limited per commercial guidelines.Unity always passes this attribute when the value is `1`, and omits it when the value is `0`.
Mobile Country code and Mobile Network Code concatenated by a dash (e.g. 310-005 ). See the list of Mobile Country Codes for more details.
Model of the device. iOS shows the device model name, for example "iphone" or "iPhone 10,1" . Android has model information such as "SAMSUNG-SM-G900A" .
Operating system of the device. Note: AppLovin sends fireos for Amazon devices.
Operating system version of the device, for example "3.1.2" .
The ratio of physical pixels to device-independent pixels. A float value from 0.74 through 4.0.
Unprocessed User-Agent string from HTTP headers
`"ua": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 10_0 like Mac OS X)``AppleWebKit/602.1.50 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/14A345"`
The web browser user agent string.
Width of the screen in physical pixels. This may be dependent on the device orientation. Note: This can differ from banner.w .
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
Unique ID of the bid request
A Unity-generated ID. This ID must be returned in the [bid response object](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/bid-responses.md).
Array of Impression objects representing the impressions offered (see Impression object ). This array contains one impression object.
For more information, refer to the section on [`impression objects`](#imp).
Unity supports one `imp` object per bid request.
A Banner object (see Banner object ). This is required if this impression is a banner ad opportunity.
For more information, refer to the section on [`banner` objects](#banner).
An object that describes a banner display impression.Unity only passes this attribute for banner and display ads.
List of supported API frameworks for this impression. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.6 for details. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.

The banner API frameworks supported by the publisher. Unity supports MRAID 3.0 (`6`). For a complete list of supported values, refer to table **5.6 API Frameworks** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).
Blocked creative attributes for banner. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.3 for details.

An array of blocked banner creative attributes. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.3** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).Unity's policy is to block the following by default:- `[1]` Audio Ad (auto-play) - `[3]` Expandable (automatic) - `[5]` Expandable (user initiated - rollover) - `[6]` In-Banner video ad (auto-play) - `[8]` Pop (for example: Over, Under, or Upon Exit) - `[9]` Provocative or Suggestive Imagery
An array of integers indicating blocked types of banners. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.2 for details.

Array of format objects representing the banner sizes permitted. Height ( h ) and width ( w ) available to pass. If none are specified, AppLovin recommends that you use the Bidrequest.imp.banner.h and Bidrequest.imp.banner.w attributes.

An array of objects representing the banner display sizes supported.Banner creative format supported sizes:- 320x50 - 728x90Display creative format supported sizes:- 250x300 - 300x250 - 320x480 - 1024x768The imp.banner object is only passed for mobile banner and interstitial display requests. If no format is specified, the dimensions default to the imp.banner.h and imp.banner.w values. If no banner format is specified, the dimensions default to the h and w values. If you have questions about supporting different dimensions, contact Unity support.
Height of the impression in pixels.
The height of the banner display, in device-independent pixels (DIPS).
A unique identifier for this object. Values usually start at 1 and increase with each object; should be unique in an impression.
Ad position on screen. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.4 for details. AppLovin RTB will always pass 1 = Above the Fold.

The banner ad's position. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.4** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).
Width of the impression in pixels.
The width of the banner display, in device-independent pixels (DIPS).
CPM minimum bid amount. Bid price must be greater than the bid floor to participate in the auction. Default currency is USD.
The minimum CPM bid required to win this impression. Expressed in USD.
The name of the ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or player responsible for rendering the ad.
AppLovin SDK version passed from the SDK, otherwise not passed.
The version of the ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or player responsible for rendering the ad.
Advisory about the number of seconds that may elapse between the auction and the actual impression. Fixed value of 14400 = 4 hours × 3600 seconds/hour.
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
The AppLovin ad unit that sent the ad request.
Support for Apple’s SKAdNetwork. See the OpenRTB SKAdNetwork extension for more details.
no, only sent to DSP bidders
For more information, refer to the documentation on [iOS 14 support](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/ios14-support.md#impression-ext).
If a DSP has at least one `SKAdNetworkItem` in the publisher app's `Info.plist` file, Unity will include this object in the bid request. This provides the information required to create a signature.
Indicates eligibility for Auto Storekit feature.- `1` indicates imp is eligible for showing Auto Storekit. - `0` indicates imp is not eligible for showing Auto Storekit.
Indicates eligibility for Custom Product Page feature.- `1` indicates imp is eligible for showing Custom Product Page. - `0` indicates imp is not eligible for showing Custom Product Page.
A subset of SKAdNetworkItem entries in the publisher app’s Info.plist that are relevant to the DSP.
Comma-separated list of integer IABTL registration IDs to exclude from IABTL shared list.
IABTL list containing the maximum entry ID of SKAdNetwork ID.
Indicates eligibility for SKOverlay feature.- `1` indicates imp is eligible for showing SKOverlay. - `0` indicates imp is not eligible for showing SKOverlay.
ID of publisher app in Apple’s App Store. Matches app.bundle .

Version of SKAdNetwork supported. Always "2.0" or higher. Dependent on both the OS version and the SDK version. Note: With the release of SKAdNetwork 2.1, this field is deprecated in favor of BidRequest.imp.ext.skadn.versions which supports an array of version numbers.
Array of strings containing the supported SKAdNetwork versions. Always "2.0" or higher. Dependent on both the OS version and the SDK version.
IDs associated with Advanced Bidders only.
A unique identifier for the impression in the bid request. Typically the value starts with 1 , then increments up to «n» for «n» impressions.
Unity supports one `imp` object per bid request, so the `id` value is always `1`.
Indicates if impression is an interstitial opportunity. Set to 1 for full screen (interstitial), or 0 if interstitial is not available.
Banner ad requests have a value of `0`; all other placements are interstitials, with a value of `1`.
An array of Metric objects (see Metric object ).
no, only sent to DSP bidders

Type of metric presented, using exchange-curated string names. Session duration ( session_duration ) is the total time a user spent in a specific app, in seconds. Session depth ( session_depth ) is the total number of ads a user saw in a given app session. A session ends after a user closes the app. Both session depth and session depth per ad format are present in the bid request. The following represent the total number of ads per format a user saw in the app session: session_depth_banner session_depth_full session_depth_medium_rectangle session_depth_native session_depth_rewarded

Number representing the value of the metric. Not present for Viewability type. Session Depth: Set to 0.0 if the user has not yet seen an ad in their current app session, or if the user has been inactive for 30 minutes.

Source of the value using exchange-curated string names. If the exchange itself is the source (as opposed to a third party), EXCHANGE is always used unless specified otherwise. Viewability: Set to ias for Integral Ad Science (IAS); set to moat for Moat. Dependent on the partners that the publisher supports. If only one is supported, only one is passed. If both are supported, both are passed. Does not apply to Open Measurement Viewability.
A Native object (see Native object )—required if this impression a native ad opportunity.
List of supported API frameworks for this impression. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.6 for details. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.
Blocked creative attributes for the native ad. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.3 for details.

Array of tracking objects to run with the ad, in response to the declared supported methods in the request. Replaces imptrackers and jstracker , which are deprecated. See OpenRTB Spec 1.2 section 4.7: Event Trackers Request Object.
Request payload complying with the Native Ad Specification. Note that this is a string.
An array of Asset Objects. Any bid must comply with the array of elements expressed by the Exchange.
Data object for ratings, prices, etc.
Unique asset ID, assigned by exchange.

The minimum requested height of the image, in pixels. Use this option for any rescaling of images by the client. Either h or hmin should be included. If only h is included, it should be considered an exact requirement. Set for icon image with a value of 80—require 1:1 aspect ratio. Set for main image with a value of 417—require 1.91:1 aspect ratio (1200×627, 1200×628, and 800×418 recommended).
Type ID of the image element supported by the publisher. The publisher can display this information in an appropriate format. See OpenRTB Native spec 1.2 Table 7.4 and 7.5 for details.

The minimum requested width of the image, in pixels. Use this option for any rescaling of images by the client. Either w or wmin should be included. If only w is included, it should be considered an exact requirement. Set for icon image with a value of 80—require 1:1 aspect ratio. Set for main image with a value of 800—require 1.91:1 aspect ratio (1200×627, 1200×628, and 800×418 recommended).
Set to 1 if asset is required (exchange will not accept a bid without it).
The context in which the ad appears. Not used and always set to 1501 .
Set to 1 when the native ad supports buyer-specific privacy notice. Field is absent when the native ad doesn’t support custom privacy links or if support is unknown.
(see the layout types). 0 for the first ad, 1 for the second ad, and so on. This is not the sequence number of the content in the stream.
Version of the Native Ad Specification to which the request complies; set to 1.2 .
Indicates whether the user receives a reward for viewing the ad, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

Flag that indicates if the impression requires secure HTTPS URL creative assets and markup, where 0 = Non-secure, 1 = secure. If omitted, the secure state is unknown, but non-secure HTTP support can be assumed. For iOS auctions, this will always be 1 = secure.
Unity requires impressions to have secure `HTTPS URL` creative assets and markup; the value is always `1`.
Identifier for the specific ad placement or ad tag that was used to initiate the auction. For SDK bidders, the network placement ID for this impression.
A Video object (see Video object )—required if this impression is video ad opportunity.
For more information, refer to the section on [video objects](#video).
An object that describes a video impression.Unity always passes this attribute for video ads.
List of supported API frameworks for this impression. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.6 for details. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.

The supported API frameworks for this impression. A value of `7` signifies Open Measurement support. For more information, refer to the documentation on [OM extensions](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/om-extensions.md).
Blocked creative attributes. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.3 for details.

An array of blocked creative attributes. Supported VAST ad companion types. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.14 for details. Some inventory supports all companion types and others static only.
yes, only sent to DSP bidders
An array of supported end card types, including `StaticResource` (`1`), `HTMLResource` (`2`), and `IFrameResource` (`3`).
Height of the player in pixels.
The height of the video player, in device-independent pixels (DIPS).
Indicates whether the impression must be linear. This is 1 for all requests.
Indicates if the impression must be linear. For Unity Exchange, this value is always `1`.
Maximum video ad duration in seconds.
The maximum video ad duration in seconds. This value is always `30`.
Content MIME types supported. video/mp4 is supported.
The supported content MIME types, including `"video/mp4"`.
Minimum video ad duration in seconds.
The minimum video ad duration in seconds. This value is always `5`.
Placement type for the impression. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.9 for details.
Unity's supported video placement types are:- `1` indicates in-stream - `5` indicates interstitial
Allowed playback methods. If none specified, assume all are allowed. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.10 for details.
Video placement subtype for the impression. See List: Plcmt Subtypes—Video in AdCOM Specification 1.0.
yes, only sent to DSP bidders
Ad position on screen. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.4 for details.

The video ad's position. Unity Ads inventory is always set to full screen (`7`). For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.4** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).

Array of supported video bid response protocols. VAST 2, VAST 3, and VAST 4 are supported. Protocols reflect what the specific inventory source supports as some inventory only supports 2.0, others both 2.0 and 3.0. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.8 for details.
yes, only sent to DSP bidders

An array of supported video protocols. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.8** in the [OpenRTB specification](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf).Unity fully supports VAST 2.0 (2) and VAST 2.0 Wrapper (5), and might support some features of VAST 3.0 (3) and VAST 3.0 Wrapper (6). For details, check with your account manager.
If multiple ad impressions are offered in the same bid request, the sequence number will allow for the coordinated delivery of multiple creatives. For Unity Exchange, this value is always `1`.
Indicates if the video can be skipped, where:- `0` indicates the video cannot be skipped. - `1` indicates the video can be skipped.For Unity Exchange, this value is always `1`.
Number of seconds a video must play before skipping is enabled. This is only applicable if the ad is skippable
Videos of total duration greater than this number of seconds can be skippable. This is only applicable if the ad is skippable.
Indicates the start delay in seconds for pre-roll, mid-roll, or post-roll ad placements. See OpenRTB Spec 2.5 Table 5.12 for details.
Width of the player in pixels.
The width of the video player, in device-independent pixels (DIPS).
For more information, refer to the section on [`pmp objects`](#pmp).

For more information, refer to the section on [`deal objects`](#deal).
An array of `deal` objects that conveys the specific deals applicable to this impression.

An optional override of the auction type of the bid request:- `1` indicates a first-price auction. - `2` indicates a second-price auction. - `3` indicates that the value passed in `bidfloor` is the agreed-upon deal price.
A unique identifier for the direct deal.

Indicates auction eligibility for the seats named in the [`deal`](#deal) object:- `0` (default) indicates that all bids are accepted. - `1` indicates that bids are restricted to the deals specified and the terms therein.
An object that specifies any industry, legal, or governmental regulations in force for this request.
For more information, refer to the documentation on [data privacy](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/data-privacy.md#user-object-extension).
An object that specifies any industry, legal, or governmental regulations enforced for this request.
Flag indicating if the bid request is subject to the COPPA regulations established by the USA FTC.- `0` indicates no. - `1` indicates yes.Unity always sends this attribute when the value is 1.
Flag indicating if this request is subject to the CCPA regulations, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.
Flag indicating if a user granted consent, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.
Flag indicating if this request is subject to the GDPR regulations, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.
Flag indicating if the request is subject to GDPR.Unity always sends this attribute when applicable to affected regions.

Upon confirming opt-out from a LGPD-affected user, the request structure for that user's device sends a flag in the regs.ext.lgpd object with the integer value true. Unity also strips all personally identifiable information (for example: IDFA, AAID, and IP address) from the request.This attribute is always passed when applicable to affected regions. For more information on the spec, contact your Unity account manager.
See OpenRTB Extension for U.S. Privacy

Flag indicating consent for requests subject to [CCPA regulations](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa). The string format must follow the IAB's [U.S. privacy specifications](https://iabtechlab.com/standards/ccpa/).Unity always sends this attribute when applicable to affected regions.
An object that provides data about the inventory source and which entity makes the final decision.
For more information, refer to the section on [`source objects`](#source).
An object that provides data about the inventory source, and which entity makes the final decision.
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB. AppLovin passes schain in the extension with subobject ver , complete , and nodes . Refer to IAB’s spec.
Entity responsible for the final impression sale decision, where 0 = exchange, 1 = upstream source.
An identifier for the [Open Measurement](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/open-measurement.md) SDK integration. This is the same as the `name` parameter of the OMID Partner object.
The version of the [Open Measurement](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/open-measurement.md) SDK integration. This is the same as the `versionString` parameter of the OMID Partner object.

A payment chain ID string containing embedded syntax described in the [TAG Payment ID Protocol v1.0](https://www.tagtoday.net/hubfs/CAF/TAG%20Certified%20Against%20Fraud%20Guidelines%20v1%202016.pdf).
For more information, refer to the section on [schain objects](#schain).
This object represents both the links in the supply chain and an indicator for whether the supply chain is complete.
A flag indicating whether the chain contains all nodes involved in the transaction leading back to the owner of the site, app or other medium of the inventory.- `0` indicates no - `1` indicates yes.

Array of [`SupplyChainNode`](#nodes) objects in the order of the chain. In a complete supply chain, the first node represents the initial advertising system and seller ID involved in the transaction (such as the owner of the site, app, or other medium). In an incomplete supply chain, it represents the first known node. The last node represents the entity sending this bid request.

The domain name of the system that bidders connect to. This might be the operational domain of the system, if that is different from the parent corporate domain. This should be the same value as used to identify sellers in an `app-ads.txt` file if one exists.

Indicates whether this node is involved in payment flow for the inventory.- `0` indicates that this node is not involved in the payment flow. - `1` indicates that the advertising system in the asi field pays the seller in the sid field, who is responsible for paying the previous node in the chain.
The OpenRTB `RequestId` of the request as issued by this seller.

The ID associated with the seller or reseller account within the advertising system. This must contain the same value used in OpenRTB transactions. This is typically `publisher.id`. Limit this field to 64 characters in length.
Version of the supply chain specification in use, in the format of `"major.minor"`.
Maximum time, in milliseconds, to submit a bid to avoid timeout. Default is 500 ms.
Timeout value in milliseconds.Unity suggests that partners respond within 200 ms to avoid the network connection dropping.
Details about the human user of the device: the advertising audience.
For more information, refer to the documentation on [data privacy](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/data-privacy.md#user-object-extension).
An object representing the human user of the device, or audience of the ad.
Contains the name , id , and segment objects.
If applicable, contains data specific to the ad unit, entered by the publisher in the MAX Dashboard.

Contains the signal field which contains any custom data the SDK bidder collects and passes to MAX SDK via the adapter (e.g. identity token required by the network so that networks or bidders can respond to a bid request).
no, only sent to SDK bidders
Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.
0 if the user did not grant consent; 1 if the user granted consent.
Flag indicating if the end user has consented to data collection.- `0` indicates no. The device ID is changed to all zeroes, and the IP address is masked. - `1` indicates yes.
0 if the user is not subject to GDPR; 1 if the user is subject to GDPR.
AppLovin-specific device ID for each user in each app.
Bidder-generated response ID to assist with logging/tracking.
Bidder-generated response ID to assist with logging and tracking.

The currency type, using ISO currency codes. Unity supports U.S. dollars (`USD`), and other currencies such as `CNY`. Make sure this field matches the currency field defined in the `adsource` configuration, and `exchange_rate` is not empty, or else Unity will ignore the bid response.This attribute is required in the response.
ID of the bid request to which this is a response (this must match bidrequest.id ).
A Unity-generated ID passed with the bid request and returned with the bid response.This attribute is required in the response.
Reason for not bidding. Refer to List 5.24 of the OpenRTB 2.5 spec.

Reason for declining to bid. For a complete list of supported values, refer to **table 5.24** in the [OpenRTB API guide](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-5-FINAL.pdf). Also refer to the section on [No-bid responses](#nbrs).
Array of seatbid objects . To make a bid, there must be at least one.
For more information, refer to the section on [`seatbid` objects](#seatbid).

Unity Exchange allows multiple `seatbid` objects in a response, however it currently only uses one `seatbid` object array. The seatbid object chosen contains a `bid.id` equal to the `impression.id`. If multiple `seatbid` objects meet this criterion, Unity Exchange selects one randomly.This attribute is required in the response.
